title: Negative for free predators in the digestion-driven ecology: on a fresh 256^2 seed, 76% of predators that leave prey dissolve within 1200 t, none reaches another prey, and none of 47 divisions has a free parent; storing the digestion product makes predators sessile and freezes the prey
summary: Labkit run of 20261027T0325-c52-digestion-ecology-claim's world.py, defaults, seed 7 (fresh), 256^2, t=12000, with the matched predator-free twin. freepred.py measures each predator body's gap to the nearest prey body by a periodic distance transform (free = gap > 2 px) from t=2500: 14% of predator bodies are free in a frame; of 328 detachments (contact -> free) 249 end with the body dissolving while free, 60 reattach (none after moving > 10 px), 19 are free at the end; free spells last median 600 t, max 1200 t. All 47 predator divisions (splits3 rule, area >= 10) have a parent touching prey, and only 1 has a daughter free 500 t later. X replicates on this seed: twin 149 frozen prey, 0 persistent splits, 1 moving track; with predators 62 persistent prey splits, generation 5, 318 moving tracks. A variant that stores the digestion product inside predator bodies (sealed min-gate diffusion, slow decay inside, fast outside; store/world_store.py) does not free them: with satiation the predators sit still on the prey and the prey stop dividing; without a cap the store blows up; with only the product capped the predators sit one per prey and do not divide.

finding.operator: digestion-driven condensation of a conserved predator material (c52), digestion product with ~1 t lifetime
finding.control: per-body signed gap to prey over a fresh 256^2 seed; matched predator-free twin; store variant (4 screens x 4 parameter sets, 128^2)
finding.result: free 14% of bodies; 328 detachments -> 249 dissolved while free, 60 reattached, 19 free at end, 0 hops > 10 px; spells median 600 t, max 1200 t; 47 divisions, 0 free parents, 1 with a daughter free at +500 t; twin 0 vs 62 persistent prey splits

limits: One seed of the claim world. A detachment is counted when the gap first exceeds 2 px, so a predator whose prey dissolves under it counts as detached (the example in free_s7.png looks like that). Tracks are linked by one-to-one overlap at 100 t per frame and end at every split or merge, so a predator that merges into another while free is not counted as dissolved. The store screens use drive.py counts on seed 0 at 128^2 only (store/*.json: kin 0.002-0.05, qs 0.5-2, chiR 0-10, full 0/1): the store parameters were not swept widely, and a larger reversal taxis (chiR 3, 10) dissolved every predator. Conclusion for the claim: in this world a predator exists only while digesting, so I, D and E belong to the predator-on-prey pair, as c49 and c51 suspected; X is real on a third reviewer-independent seed.
